name: Prawn Balchao
subtitle: a fierce vinegar-and-chilli prawn pickle eaten a spoonful at a time

ingredients.note: small prawns hold up better than large
Goan coconut vinegar if you can find it, else cider vinegar
balances the vinegar, do not skip
a pickle needs the oil to seal it

prepNotes: Soak the chillies in the vinegar for 30 minutes before grinding. This is what makes balchao red rather than brown.
Pat the prawns bone dry on a cloth. Wet prawns weep water and the pickle will not keep.
Use a scrupulously dry glass or ceramic jar. Any water in the jar and it spoils within the week.

steps.text: Grind the soaked chillies, garlic, ginger, cumin, pepper, cloves, cinnamon and turmeric to a thick paste using only the soaking vinegar, no water.
steps.tip: No water at any stage. Vinegar is the only liquid in this recipe.

steps.text: Toss the prawns with 1/2 tsp salt and a pinch of turmeric and fry them in 2 tbsp of the oil over high heat for 2 minutes, until they just turn pink. Lift them out.
steps.tip: Two minutes only. They cook again later and rubbery prawns are the usual failure here.

steps.text: Pour the rest of the oil into the same kadhai and fry the chopped onion over medium heat for 12-15 minutes, until dark gold and jammy.
Add the ground masala and fry 10 minutes, stirring often, until the oil separates and pools clearly at the edges.
steps.tip: This is the long, unglamorous part. Under-fried masala tastes raw and sharp for days.

steps.text: Stir in the sugar and salt and cook 2 more minutes.
Return the prawns, stir to coat, and cook 3 minutes on low.
Take it off the heat and cool completely, uncovered, in the pan.
Pack into a dry jar, pressing down so the oil covers the surface. Leave 2 days before eating.
steps.tip: It is harsh on day one and rounded by day three. Wait.

storage: Keeps 3 weeks refrigerated as long as a film of oil covers the top and you only ever use a dry spoon. Serve at room temperature with rice and dal or in a pav.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Ingredients given to taste rather than by weight are counted as zero, so the real figure is a little higher than this. The + says so.
